nodes.binding: Assess DVD identity for the specific object tracked from the source image using shape, location, and surrounding context. Do not infer identity solely because an edited object is a white disc; report uncertainty if the source object cannot confidently be identified or matched.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

d2: The binding overweights uncertainty about whether the source item is truly a DVD and whether the edited disc is the same object. The source image shows a small rectangular, printed item near the center; the edit shows a white disc at that location, while a separate white disc appears on the dark object to the right. This is evidence of a likely transformation, but the trace does not establish which disc corresponds to the source item. Keep identity and correspondence as distinct checks: assess spatial/scene correspondence and visible change, and use unknown only when those cannot be resolved—not merely because the source is not unmistakably a DVD. Conversely, do not treat a nearby white disc alone as proof of a successful edit. The reference “no” is an aggregate constraint, not atomic ground truth; the rubric’s “no progress” versus “partial progress” distinction may be ambiguous here, so inspect whether the node’s criterion captures requested progress rather than only post-edit DVD identity. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported; this is a visual-evidence and criterion-resolution issue.

The source shows a small printed rectangular item on the snow near center; the edit has a white disc near that location and another white disc on the dark object to the right. Do not require the source to be unmistakably identifiable as a DVD, but do not count a nearby or newly appearing white disc as proof of recoloring. Reserve unknown for genuinely unresolved correspondence or visibility, rather than defaulting to it when the object’s label is uncertain.
